stories.title: DWF supports Sustainable Investments Group growth
555 Expert witness survey highlights key trends
stories.ltme_summary: Bond Solon, with the Law Society Gazette, has published its expert witness survey, conducted online from 2 to 25 September 2026 with 555 respondents. The survey reports pressure on fees, payment delays, AI use and standards, and says respondents want clearer AI protocols and some form of accreditation or regulation.
stories.hook: Bond Solon survey of 555 expert witnesses finds fee pressure and AI concerns, with mixed views on regulation

stories.title: The new client: Claude
stories.ltme_summary: A junior solicitor writing in Solicitors Journal describes how clients increasingly consult AI before instructing lawyers, bringing challenges around trust, privilege and costs. The column says uploading confidential documents to public AI platforms may compromise confidentiality and privilege, and that clients sometimes ask for second opinions from AI on counsel's advice.
stories.hook: Junior solicitor warns that clients arriving with AI-drafted cases create privilege and confidentiality risks

stories.title: Law Society of Scotland informs MPs on Lord Advocate inquiry
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society of Scotland told the Scottish Affairs Committee that any reform of the Lord Advocate's dual role must be evidence-led and consulted on widely. Michael Clancy, its Director of Law Reform, gave oral evidence on 4 November. The Society has not taken a final position and says its inquiry evidence could inform Lord Boyd's Scottish Government review.
stories.hook: Law Society of Scotland urges evidence-led reform of the Lord Advocate's dual role before MPs

stories.title: New law helps young people find jobs
Harvey + Legora IPO Plans, A&O $1.1bn, Legal Innovators NY
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer's weekly wrap reports that Harvey and Legora are each reported to be in early IPO discussions with advisers. Legora's spokesperson said it does not comment on speculation, though CEO Max Junestrand has long said he wants to list one day. The piece links possible listings to a risk of AI valuation correction and notes Big Tech moves into legal.
stories.hook: Harvey and Legora are both reported to be sounding out IPO advisers, with Legora declining to comment on timing

stories.title: The mentorship questions law students should ask during recruitment
Litera and filerskeepers Bridge the Gap Between Global Retention Requirements and Records Governance
stories.hook: Litera and filerskeepers pair retention law intelligence with FileTrail disposition, extending governance into SharePoint

stories.title: Introducing SimpleDocs 360: AI-Native Contract Lifecycle Management
stories.ltme_summary: SimpleDocs, the Miami provider of AI contract solutions and parent of Law Insider, has launched SimpleDocs 360, an AI-native contract lifecycle management platform. According to the company, it combines three products, SimpleAI, Workflow and Repository, and integrates with tools including Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Word and DocuSign. CEO Preston Clark says it was built for the AI era. Hundreds of enterprise customers are said to already use SimpleDocs.
stories.hook: SimpleDocs says its new SimpleDocs 360 platform brings contract requests, drafting and repository work into one AI-native CLM

stories.title: A&O Shearman to devote billable hours to building AI tools as part of $1 billion investment
stories.ltme_summary: A&O Shearman plans to put more than 5 per cent of annual revenue into AI over five years, a $1.1bn (£800m) investment. Lawyers in every practice will be asked to set aside at least 3 per cent of billable time to help build specialist AI tools. Global managing partner Hervé Ekué says the firm wants lawyers at the centre of AI development rather than relying only on ready-made products.
stories.hook: A&O Shearman will ask every lawyer to give 3 per cent of billable time to building its own AI tools

stories.title: ‘I think my supervisor is trying to sabotage my career. Should I quit?’
Startup Corner: Lawfecta looks to AI to solve law firms’ legal talent needs
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider's startup corner profiles Lawfecta, which is said to use AI to address law firms' legal talent needs. The extract available is only a site verification page, so the substance of the piece cannot be confirmed from what was supplied. The story is likely a profile of an early-stage company rather than a deal or launch.
stories.hook: Lawfecta is pitching AI at law firms' talent shortages, according to Legal IT Insider's startup profile

stories.title: Addleshaw Goddard adds McDermott PE partner trio as hiring push gathers pace
‘A real sense of loss’: Leaders reflect after closure of firm
stories.ltme_summary: Berwins Solicitors, a Harrogate firm founded 40 years ago with around 40 staff, has entered administration after filing a notice of appointment. Managing director Danielle Day confirmed the appointment on LinkedIn. No reasons for the closure have been given, and accounts to June 2025 showed net assets of almost £300,000.
stories.hook: Harrogate firm Berwins Solicitors enters administration after 40 years, with no reasons given for closure

stories.title: We will change - but it will cost you, says LSB
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board has welcomed an independent review by Richard Lloyd of legal services regulation, which the government has accepted in full. LSB chair Monisha Shah says the regulator will set out a 2027-30 strategy and warns that change needs strategic investment, with a budget consultation to follow. Blind Justice UK criticises the review for not covering the SRA or setting a timetable.
stories.hook: Legal Services Board welcomes Lloyd review of legal regulation but says change will need strategic investment

stories.title: In depth: Bond Solon/Gazette Expert Witness Survey 2026 - key takeaways
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette, with Bond Solon, publishes key findings from its 2026 expert witness survey of 555 experts. AI use has risen, with 12 per cent saying they use it regularly and 23 per cent occasionally, while 73 per cent cite over-reliance on AI as a concern. Most respondents back formal regulation of expert witnesses, by 51 per cent to fewer than one in four opposed.
stories.hook: Expert witness survey finds AI use rising, with 73 per cent of 555 experts worried about over-reliance

stories.title: AI use by litigants in person adding to courts burden, LCJ warns
stories.ltme_summary: The lady chief justice, Baroness Carr of Walton-on-the-Hill, says in her third annual judiciary report that litigants in person are increasingly using AI to build claims, placing significant demands on court staff and judges. The report, covering October 2025 to September 2026, says the Court of Appeal Criminal Division is preparing guidance on AI in grounds of appeal and that oversight of AI use will remain judge-led.
stories.hook: Lady chief justice says litigants in person using AI are adding to court demands, with CACD guidance on AI in appeals coming

stories.title: Claims firm's losses double to £4.8m - but caseload 'exceptionally strong'
stories.ltme_summary: Manchester claims firm Veritas Solicitors reports that its operating losses more than doubled to £4.8m for the year to 29 November 2025, with turnover down 8 per cent to around £9m. Its members' report says the current caseload could yield £134m if settled. The accounts show £63.9m owed, net liabilities of £30m and a debtor, I Quote, that says it cannot make further payments.
stories.hook: Veritas Solicitors' operating losses double to £4.8m as it points to £134m from its caseload

stories.title: Former state official charged with tampering bar exam results
stories.ltme_summary: Arkansas prosecutors have charged Nancie Givens, former executive director of the Arkansas Supreme Court's Office of Professional Programs, with 65 felony counts. The state supreme court says an investigation found irregularities in bar exam results from 2020 to 2025, with 11,400 files deleted or unavailable.
stories.hook: Former Arkansas bar office director faces 65 felony counts over exam tampering

stories.title: 2 BigLaw firms face proposed class actions over cyber breaches
Biglaw’s Best-Paid Partners Now Live In Silicon Valley, Sorry Manhattan
Why MCP Could Be A Hero For Your Lean Legal Team
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law is promoting a webinar on 12 November, hosted with Generate and Brightflag, on using Model Context Protocol (MCP) in lean legal operations teams. Michelle Garza of Generate and Anna Richards of Brightflag will cover how MCP works, answering spend and vendor questions, and managing AI tool permissions.
stories.hook: Generate and Brightflag webinar pitches MCP as a tool for lean legal ops teams

US Charges 3 Over $129M AI Scam Using Fake UK Lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: US prosecutors have charged three people over an alleged $129m artificial intelligence scam that used fake UK lawyers, according to a Law360 Pulse Legal Tech headline. The extract is only a summary line, so details of the charges, defendants and the scheme are not available here.
stories.hook: Three charged in US over $129m AI scam using fake UK lawyers

stories.title: Cravath makes rare London partner promotion amid 11-strong round
stories.ltme_summary: Cravath has promoted Lawrence Verhelst, a London counsel focused on finance and capital markets, to partner as part of an 11-strong round. Legal Business says it is the firm's largest partner promotions round since 2020. Verhelst joined as an associate in 2014 and has been European counsel since late 2021.
stories.hook: Cravath makes one London partner in its largest promotions round since 2020

stories.title: Catching the pro bono bug: Lloyds and Societe Generale among new sign-ups as In House Pro Bono Pledge reaches 25
Full details: the five-partner Weil team joining Kirkland with Ramona Nee
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Ramona Nee, a Boston-based private equity partner and co-head of Weil's US PE practice, is joining Kirkland & Ellis in the New Year with five further partners from Weil's M&A and finance groups. The team totals 40 lawyers, according to the report.
stories.hook: Ramona Nee and five partners move from Weil to Kirkland in January

stories.title: Harvey held preliminary meetings with Latham advisors over potential listing
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business understands that Harvey has held preliminary meetings with its regular advisers Latham & Watkins about a possible future listing. The report says the talks were preliminary and that Harvey has no imminent IPO plans. The discussions were first reported by Business Insider.
stories.hook: Harvey has held early IPO talks with Latham & Watkins, sources say

stories.title: Kirkland hires 40-strong Weil team led by Ramona Nee
stories.ltme_summary: Kirkland & Ellis has hired a 40-lawyer PE, M&A and debt finance team from Weil, led by Ramona Nee, according to Kirkland's announcement. The group joins in January 2027 and includes six partners. Kirkland's executive committee chair Jon Ballis praised the hires.
stories.hook: Kirkland hires 40-lawyer Weil team led by Ramona Nee for January 2027 start

stories.title: Slaughters and HSF Kramer join legal line-up for Anthropic IPO
Cravath promotes one in London in 11-strong partner round
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that Cravath has promoted London lawyer Lawrence Verhelst to partner in an 11-strong global round, taking its London partnership to eight. The firm's average profit per partner was $7.2m last year, per The American Lawyer. Verhelst joins on 1 January.
stories.hook: Cravath makes Lawrence Verhelst partner in London, lifting its London partnership to eight

stories.title: Peers condemn use of 'Henry VIII' powers in jury trial bill
stories.ltme_summary: A House of Lords Delegated Powers committee has criticised the Courts and Tribunals Bill for giving ministers power, under Clause 3(5), to add offences to the list tried without a jury through secondary legislation. The committee wants that change made in primary legislation. The bill goes to a Lords bill committee on Tuesday.
stories.hook: Lords committee says jury trial limits should not be set by secondary legislation
entities: House of Lords Delegated Powers and Regulatory Reform Committee

stories.title: Minesoft Origin vs PatSnap vs Questel Orbit: Which Platform Fits Your Team?
Form: Make a claim with others to an employment tribunal: Form ET1A
stories.ltme_summary: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has uploaded a Welsh translated version of Form ET1A, used to make a joint claim to an employment tribunal. The form page was updated on 6 November 2026, following an amended English form dated 30 October 2026.
stories.hook: HMCTS uploads Welsh version of joint employment tribunal claim form ET1A

stories.title: FTI Consulting hires former Eversheds Sutherland CEO
stories.ltme_summary: LegalTechTalk reports that FTI Consulting has appointed former Eversheds Sutherland chief executive Mark Wasserman as a Senior Managing Director. He will advise law firms and corporate legal departments.
stories.hook: FTI Consulting appoints former Eversheds Sutherland CEO Mark Wasserman as Senior Managing Director

stories.title: Subpoenas Are Coming: Washington Law Firms Are Getting Ready For A Congressional Probe Boom
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports that Democratic wins in both chambers will bring congressional investigations, with lawyers in Washington preparing. Brian Nieves and Mark Epley expect more investigators, and Cooley's Susanne Grooms warned the volume could double. Nine law firms that agreed to provide $940 million in free legal services to Trump may be targets, according to the piece.
stories.hook: Washington firms prepare for a surge in congressional probes after Democrats take both chambers

stories.title: Harmeet Heads For The Hills
From Biglaw To Boutique: Tyka’s Co-Chair Shares His Thoughts On Building A New Firm
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law interviews Ben Eggert, co-chair of Tyka, an insurance boutique launched by 21 attorneys from Wiley Rein. Eggert says the firm brought over 50 clients and 1,500 matters and describes the work of setting up document management and billing. The interview covers client retention through the transition.
stories.hook: Tyka's Ben Eggert says the 21-lawyer Wiley Rein spin-off took more than 50 clients and 1,500 matters

stories.title: Bar Exam Official Charged With 65 Felonies, Accused Of Playing Robin Hood With Test Scores
iManage Puts A Firm’s Institutional Knowledge To Work For Agentic AI
stories.ltme_summary: iManage has described its next generation platform, released in October, which adds AI features to its document management system. Paul Walker, Global Solutions Director, demonstrated for Above the Law how a calendar Get Ready button builds meeting briefings, how Playbooks check batches of documents against review standards, and how citations link back to source documents. iManage says it stores about 30 billion documents for 3,500 customers.
stories.hook: iManage says its October platform release uses AI to turn stored firm documents into meeting briefings and batch contract reviews

stories.ltme_summary: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang and other NVIDIA officers and directors have moved to dismiss a shareholder derivative suit brought by Berliner. The suit rests on a novel theory of copyright risk, according to the commentary.

stories.ltme_summary: Cooley reports that partner Susanne Grooms spoke to Reuters about a likely surge in congressional investigations after Democrats won both chambers in the midterms, and said the volume could double. The post links to the Reuters piece and lists earlier press mentions.
stories.hook: Cooley's Susanne Grooms says congressional investigations could double after Democrats win both chambers

stories.title: Travis LeBlanc Named to Forbes’ Inaugural America’s Top Lawyers for AI List // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.ltme_summary: Cooley says Forbes has named its partner Travis LeBlanc to the inaugural America's Top Lawyers for AI list. LeBlanc co-chairs Cooley's global cyber, data and privacy practice and advises on cybersecurity, data privacy, telecommunications and emerging technology regulation. According to the announcement, Forbes selected honorees through a multistage editorial process assessing the significance and complexity of their AI-related work, broader practice and thought leadership.
stories.hook: Cooley's Travis LeBlanc named to Forbes' first America's Top Lawyers for AI list

stories.title: HHS Finalizes Deregulatory Overhaul of ONC Health IT Certification Program | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: Morrison Foerster reports that HHS, through ONC, has finalised the HTI-5 rule, which substantially cuts requirements under the ONC Health IT Certification Program. The firm is summarising the regulator's action for its healthcare readers.
stories.hook: HHS finalises HTI-5 rule, cutting requirements under the ONC Health IT Certification Program

stories.title: AI Model Governance for Legal Teams: A Working Framework
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic publishes a guide to AI model governance for general counsel and legal operations leaders. It sets out what a defensible framework contains, including an inventory, use-case classification, deployment controls, versioned records and monitoring. The guide cites the ABA technology section and a State Bar generative AI framework.
stories.hook: Neota Logic sets out a framework for governing legal AI models, from inventory to retirement

stories.title: Sarah Irwin On The AI Issue GCs Should Fix First | Summize
stories.ltme_summary: Sarah Irwin of ITGC, a community for in-house legal teams, writes on Summize's site about AI accuracy for general counsel. She cites a survey of 82 European in-house leaders in which 70 per cent named accuracy as their top AI concern. She also cites Summize's AI Fluency Report, based on 505 US in-house professionals, which found 14.5 per cent connect AI to approved internal knowledge.
stories.hook: Summize-hosted essay says only 14.5 per cent of in-house teams connect AI to approved internal knowledge

stories.title: Time | Track Every Billable Hour, Automatically | Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite promotes Always-On Time, which it says captures 10 to 15 per cent more billable time. A UK partner describes moving from handwritten notes to recording a full day. The page is vendor marketing with a customer testimonial.
stories.hook: Thomson Reuters Elite says Always-On Time captures 10 to 15 per cent more billable time for firms

stories.title: Proforma | Turn Proforma Review into a Billing Accelerator | Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite promotes Proforma and cites its 2026 Cloud Results Report, which draws on more than 120 law firms. The report says firms that moved finance operations to the cloud cut days sales outstanding and shortened month-end close. The page is vendor marketing.
stories.hook: Thomson Reuters Elite's 2026 Cloud Results Report links cloud finance to faster collections at 120 law firms

Topics include a count of 2,266 AI hallucination cases, a Californian data breach register where social engineering is a common cause, and a judge's remarks on grace toward opposing counsel. The post is commentary on other reports.

‘Start telling us now about AI use’, top judge urges experts
stories.ltme_summary: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith told the Bond Solon Expert Witness Conference that experts should declare AI use now, before a rule requires it. She co-chaired the Civil Justice Council working group whose report last week recommended a declaration where AI shaped the substantive content of an expert report. She said the duties of independence and objectivity have not changed.
stories.hook: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith tells experts to declare AI use now, ahead of a CJC-recommended rule

stories.title: Your AI can now update the deal, not just read it
stories.ltme_summary: Legatics says its MCP connector now supports write actions, letting connected AI assistants create matters, update checklist items, add comments and reassign work in live deal files. Changes sit under existing user permissions and appear in the audit trail.
